rationale: Split into five feature modules ordered by dependency: shared contracts and utilities first, key/backends next, then JWS signatures, then JWT claim handling built on JWS, and finally JWE plus public package integration. This catches format/constant/import contract mistakes before cryptographic features depend on them, catches key abstraction defects before signing, and leaves the final milestone to verify the complete documented public surface and end-to-end JOSE workflows.

milestones.title: Shared JOSE constants, exceptions, utilities, and packaging
milestones.objective: Create the installable jose package foundation: pyproject metadata/dependencies, constants, exception hierarchy, and reusable utility functions for JSON and base64url byte handling.
milestones.risk_rationale: This milestone delivers the cross-module contracts that every later feature imports: algorithm names, zip constants, error classes, and byte/base64 helpers. Its gate can verify these directly by importing the package modules, checking exported constants/classes, and exercising utility encoding/decoding without requiring JWK, JWS, JWT, or JWE implementations.

criteria: The project is installable as a Python package named python-jose with dependencies declared for cryptography, pycryptodome, rsa, ecdsa, pyasn1, and pytest.
jose.constants exports algorithm and compression registries used by all JOSE modules.
jose.exceptions defines a common JOSEError base class and feature-specific JWTError, JWSError, JWKError, JWEError, and JWEParseError subclasses.
jose.utils provides deterministic base64url encode/decode helpers that operate on bytes and strings without padding in encoded output.
corner_cases: Base64url decoding accepts unpadded input whose length requires padding restoration.
Utility helpers reject or fail clearly on malformed base64url input.
Exception subclasses can be caught through JOSEError.
Importing jose.constants, jose.exceptions, and jose.utils succeeds in a clean environment before later modules are implemented.

agents.title: Specification test author
agents.mandate: Write executable tests from the PRD and architecture for package installation metadata, jose.constants exports, exception inheritance, and base64url utility behavior. Do not modify source.

agents.title: Contract author
agents.mandate: Implement the shared constants, exception hierarchy, utility functions, minimal package files, and pyproject dependency/configuration contract that later JOSE modules will import.

agents.title: Specification auditor
agents.mandate: Review the shared substrate against the design documents, especially exported constant names, exception names, pyproject dependencies, and utility byte/string behavior. Report deviations without editing.

agents.title: Implementer
agents.mandate: Fix only the shared-contract deviations reported by the reviewer while preserving the exported names that later milestones will import.

milestones.title: JWK management and cryptographic key backends
milestones.objective: Implement key abstractions, backend key classes, random byte support, and JWK construction/import/export for HMAC, RSA, EC, AES, oct, and key-set use cases.
milestones.risk_rationale: This milestone delivers the key layer consumed by JWS, JWT, and JWE. Its gate can verify key creation, parsing, import/export, backend selection, and key-set lookup using jose.jwk and jose.backends directly, without needing token signing or encryption modules that come later.

criteria: jose.backends exposes RSAKey, ECKey, HMACKey, AESKey, DIRKey, and get_random_bytes following the fallback behavior described in the architecture.
jose.backends.base defines the shared Key interface and DIRKey direct key-management implementation.
jose.backends.native provides a usable HMACKey and NativeHMACKey-compatible implementation for HS256, HS384, and HS512 signing and verification.
jose.jwk exposes Key and construct(), and can construct appropriate key objects from raw secrets, JWK dictionaries, JWK sets, and documented algorithm names.
JWK import/export preserves required fields such as kty, kid, alg, use, key material fields, and public/private distinction where applicable.
corner_cases: Unknown kty or unsupported algorithm raises JWKError instead of returning an unusable object.
JWK sets with multiple keys can select by kid when a kid is supplied.
Missing kid in a multi-key set fails clearly instead of choosing a random key.
HMAC secrets are accepted as str and bytes and produce equivalent verification behavior.
RSA and EC backend imports degrade according to the documented fallback rules if an optional backend is unavailable.

agents.title: Specification test author
agents.mandate: Write executable tests for backend exports, Key/DIRKey/HMACKey behavior, get_random_bytes, jwk.construct with raw secrets, JWK dictionaries, and JWK sets. Do not modify source.

agents.title: Contract author
agents.mandate: Implement the backend Key contract, DIRKey, backend package exports, native HMAC key behavior, and random byte helper while preserving constants/exceptions from the previous milestone.

agents.title: Implementer
agents.mandate: Implement jose.jwk key construction, key-set selection, JWK import/export, and cryptography/rsa/ecdsa backend adapters required for RSA, EC, AES, oct, and direct key use.

agents.title: Edge-case hardener
agents.mandate: Harden key parsing and backend behavior for unsupported algorithms, malformed JWKs, multi-key JWK sets, str/bytes secrets, and optional-backend fallback paths.

milestones.title: JWS signing and verification
milestones.objective: Implement compact JWS signing, verification, header handling, payload serialization, and algorithm enforcement using the key layer.
milestones.risk_rationale: This milestone delivers digital signatures independently of JWT claims. Its gate can sign and verify payloads through jose.jws using HMAC/RSA/EC keys from the frozen key layer, check compact-token formatting, and verify tamper rejection without depending on JWT claim validation or JWE encryption.

criteria: jws.sign(payload, key, headers=None, algorithm=ALGORITHMS.HS256) returns a compact three-segment JWS string.
jws.verify(token, key, algorithms, verify=True) validates signatures and returns the original payload bytes.
Header algorithm selection is enforced against the allowed algorithms argument.
Payloads supplied as dict, str, or bytes are serialized consistently and recoverable as bytes.
Tampered payload, tampered signature, malformed compact serialization, and unsupported algorithms raise JWSError.
corner_cases: alg='none' is not accepted unless explicitly supported by the documented contract.
A token with fewer or more than three compact segments is rejected.
Verification with algorithms as a single string behaves the same as a one-item list.
verify=False returns payload bytes without requiring signature verification but still parses compact JWS safely.
Custom headers are preserved in the protected header without overriding the selected alg incorrectly.

agents.title: Specification test author
agents.mandate: Write executable tests for compact JWS signing, verification, algorithm allow-list enforcement, payload serialization, header inspection, malformed token handling, and tamper rejection. Do not modify source.

agents.title: Implementer
agents.mandate: Implement jose.jws directly from the design documents using the frozen constants, exceptions, utilities, jwk.construct, and backend key contracts.

agents.title: Gate repairer
agents.mandate: If the milestone gate fails, fix exactly the reported JWS behavior or exported-symbol failures without changing earlier frozen contracts except where required to preserve compatibility.

milestones.title: JWT encode/decode and registered claim validation
milestones.objective: Implement JWT token generation and verification on top of JWS, including standard registered claims, options, leeway, audience, issuer, subject, jti, and at_hash handling.
milestones.risk_rationale: This milestone delivers authentication-token behavior that builds on the frozen JWS layer. Its gate can encode and decode signed JWTs, inspect unverified claims/headers, and verify claim-validation failures without needing JWE or final package re-export wiring.

criteria: jwt.encode(claims, key, algorithm=ALGORITHMS.HS256, headers=None, access_token=None) returns a signed compact JWT string.
jwt.decode(token, key, algorithms=None, options=None, audience=None, issuer=None, subject=None, access_token=None) verifies the signature and returns a claims dictionary.
Datetime exp, iat, and nbf values are serialized to numeric dates during encode.
decode validates exp, nbf, iat, aud, iss, sub, jti, and at_hash according to options and explicit arguments.
get_unverified_header and get_unverified_claims expose token data without signature verification for inspection workflows.
corner_cases: Expired tokens fail unless leeway permits them.
Tokens with nbf in the future fail unless leeway permits them.
Audience can be a string or list, and missing audience handling follows verification options.
Issuer can be a string or list.
Subject mismatch raises JWTError.
Malformed numeric date values raise JWTError instead of being silently accepted.
access_token plus at_hash mismatch raises JWTError.
options can disable individual claim checks without disabling unrelated checks.

agents.title: Specification test author
agents.mandate: Write executable tests for jwt.encode/decode, registered claim validation, options, leeway, audience/issuer/subject handling, at_hash behavior, datetime conversion, and unverified accessors. Do not modify source.

agents.title: Implementer
agents.mandate: Implement jose.jwt directly from the PRD and architecture using the frozen JWS signing/verification API and shared constants/exceptions/utilities.

agents.title: Gate repairer
agents.mandate: If the milestone gate fails, fix exactly the reported JWT encode/decode, claim validation, or exported-symbol failures without changing the frozen JWS public contract.

milestones.title: JWE encryption/decryption and unified public API integration
milestones.objective: Implement compact JWE encryption/decryption, enforce JWE limits and options, wire jose.__init__ public exports, and verify the complete documented python-jose API surface end to end.
milestones.risk_rationale: This final milestone delivers confidentiality features and integrates all modules at their documented import paths. Its gate verifies JWE behavior directly and then grades the full public contract: from jose imports for jwt, jws, jwk, jwe, utils, ALGORITHMS, ZIPS, exception classes, backend key classes, NativeHMACKey, verify, Key, plus end-to-end JWT/JWS/JWE/JWK workflows.

criteria: jwe.encrypt(plaintext, key, encryption=ALGORITHMS.A256GCM, algorithm=ALGORITHMS.DIR, zip=None, cty=None, kid=None) returns a compact JWE token as bytes or a documented bytes-compatible value.
jwe.decrypt(token, key) parses, authenticates, decrypts, and returns the original plaintext bytes.
JWE protected headers include alg, enc, and optional zip, cty, and kid fields.
Direct symmetric JWE with A256GCM works using supported oct/AES key material.
Compression using documented ZIPS values works when requested and rejects unsupported zip values.
Tokens larger than JWE_SIZE_LIMIT are rejected with JWEError or JWEParseError.
jose.__init__ exposes the documented unified API modules, constants, exceptions, backend key classes, NativeHMACKey, jws.verify, jwk.Key, and version information.
The visible check_tests suite and the milestone behavioral suite pass together.
corner_cases: Malformed compact JWE with the wrong number of segments raises JWEParseError.
Tampered ciphertext, IV, tag, encrypted key, or protected header fails authentication and does not return plaintext.
Decrypting with the wrong key raises JWEError.
Plaintext may be str or bytes and decrypts to the original byte content.
Unsupported key-management or content-encryption algorithms fail clearly.
The package contains only the jose top-level package required by the design and no duplicate implementation package.
Public imports from jose work in a clean interpreter without requiring private-module import order.

agents.title: Specification test author
agents.mandate: Write executable tests for JWE encrypt/decrypt, malformed/tampered token failures, size-limit enforcement, compression/header options, and all documented root-level jose imports. Do not modify source.

agents.mandate: Implement jose.jwe and wire jose.__init__ so every documented module, function, class, constant, exception, backend key, NativeHMACKey, verify, Key, and version export is reachable at the public import path.
